title: GIS-Based EV Charging Station Suitability Model for Eindhoven
goal: Develop a GIS-based suitability model to identify the most appropriate locations for new public EV charging stations within the Municipality of Eindhoven, Netherlands.
context: Electric vehicle charging infrastructure requires careful planning to ensure that new charging stations are both accessible and capable of meeting future demand. Geographic Information Systems (GIS) provide an effective way to support this planning by combining multiple spatial datasets into a single decision-making process. In this session, publicly available datasets will be collected, prepared, and standardized for the study area. Spatial analysis techniques such as clipping, buffering, proximity analysis, and suitability modelling will then be applied to evaluate each criterion before combining them into a final suitability map that highlights the most appropriate candidate locations.

session_goal_achievement.Why or why not: Yes, but it took a little longer than 1 hour, although Claude did help a lot.

nodes.label: Diagnose NoData propagation and prescribe a re-rasterize fix
nodes.detail: Claude explains that NoData propagates through any raster calculation regardless of the formula used, meaning the whole overlay result was being wiped out; the fix is to re-rasterize the water mask with a genuine 0 background value instead of NoData.

nodes.detail: The participant re-rasterizes the water layer: a first attempt with NoData set to -9999 still yields only 1-values, so she re-runs it as Claude suggested, with NoData left unset and the output pre-initialized to 0, renames the result as the water mask, re-runs her native Raster Calculator expression (AHP_result * (water_mask == 0)), and confirms the output as the final masked suitability raster.
